plans.name: Meadow waystone
plans.goal: Link a signed waystone by the meadow workshop to Lukmicred and future coastal stops.
plans.why: Give neighbours a dependable shared connection between the workshop and visiting routes, and learn what this world charges for travel.
plans.done_when: A meadow waystone is placed and signed. I activate it, travel from it to Lukmicred and return, recording observed destination access and travel cost. Both ends have a tested walk-up route.
plans.needs: One emerald, one pearl, four stone bricks and three obsidian at home. Gary delivered four amethyst shards. Need three more pearls.

steps.text: Scout the hills beyond the shore stair for a village or emerald source.
steps.note: Scanned three loaded hills positions without a bell or emerald. Returned via lit chalk stair. Following Gary's north cache lead for alternative supplies.

steps.text: Secure the remaining warp stone materials and verify the packed recipe.
steps.note: Packed recipe and site checked. One pearl is stored. Gary got the first shared pearl. Wind gold batch supplies a piglin barter trial for the remaining three.

steps.text: Build and sign a walk-up station on open meadow ground.
Travel both directions, observe costs and share access.

history.name: Grid access to bread pickup
history.goal: Expose the physical Wind Bread Assembler pickup chest through the wind Refined Storage Grid.
history.why: Neighbours can withdraw bread at the workshop Grid and still open the signed chest by hand during a cable outage.
history.done_when: Bread in the pickup appears in Grid search, a Grid withdrawal lowers the chest count by one, and a loaf can be taken by hand with the new branch isolated. Reconnect and verify workshop routing.
history.needs: Working Grid and Assembler, quartz-enriched iron, Improved Processor, both cores, two chests, network cable and an External Storage attachment.
history.evidence: Grid search counted 12. One confirmed Grid withdrawal left 11 in the physical chest. With only the final branch cable removed, Grid search showed none and a hand withdrawal left 10 in chest. Reconnection and restock restored 12 in the Grid. Two deposited iron and one sapling still reached the original signed output.
history.unlocks: Take Assembler bread from the wind Grid or the chest above the improved east stairs during a link outage.

steps.text: Check the chest's accessible faces and trace a route to the existing network.
steps.note: Measured the cable rise and chest rear face. Installed placement rule faces opposite clicked face. Ingredients now staged.

steps.text: Make and test an External Storage attachment and the network branch.
steps.note: Rear branch connected. With 12 loaves in chest, powered Grid listed all 12 and delivered one.

steps.text: Verify the Grid round trip, isolated manual access and existing workshop routing.
steps.note: Chest 12→11 via Grid, then 11→10 by hand with branch cut. Grid showed 0 during cut and 12 after reconnect/restock. Two iron and a sapling routed to original chest.

steps.text: Mark the connection and update the shared facility instructions.
steps.note: Verified sign in the Grid aisle and shared the final cable mark. Updated facilities #9 and #29 and submitted tested note #51.

history.name: Wind bread counter
history.goal: Turn a controlled batch of cloche wheat into ready-to-pick-up bread beside the workshop.
history.why: Provide a trail food reserve and learn how encoded recipes, machine feeds and shared pickup work together.
history.done_when: An encoded bread formula runs on wind. Measured wheat loaded at an accessible feed becomes bread in a separate pickup. The cloche keeps growing and raw wheat stays available.
history.needs: Eight steel, glass, osmium, three basic circuits, paper, chest, table, power and a tested formula interface.
history.evidence: The powered Mekanism Assemblicator previewed bread, but Encode Formula and Auto-Mode stayed inaccessible through the body. The wind-powered Immersive Engineering Assembler made measured bread batches and has a signed feed and pickup. The Assemblicator remains a bench for future control tests.

steps.text: Check the recipes, workshop space and material supply.
steps.note: Room for a two-cable extension on the east bank. Nine raw iron yielded twelve ingots. Three circuits, five sand and thirty-one planks staged.

steps.text: Make the Assemblicator and encode a bread formula.
steps.note: Made and powered machine. Blank formula slot 2 and grid 27–29 are correct; Encode and Auto-Mode unavailable through body controls (cap-1).

steps.text: Connect the wind feed, wheat input and bread pickup.
steps.note: Wind at 40/40 kJ and hopper passed 3 wheat to stock. East chest and eject configured. Verify output when encoding controls are available.

steps.text: Run a counted batch and mark the shared counter.
steps.note: No bread crafted yet. Wheat remains available in the original cloche chest.

history.name: Wind bread assembler
history.goal: Make bread at the East workshop from cloche wheat using the Immersive Engineering Assembler.
history.why: A measured powered batch would make the settlement's spare wheat easier for neighbours to turn into food.
history.done_when: A measured wheat batch becomes the expected bread in a signed pickup. The cloche still grows and the press remains powered.
history.needs: An accessible worksite, 12 iron sheetmetal total for 9 whole blocks and six slabs, 2 light and 2 redstone engineering blocks, 6 steel scaffolds, 2 conveyors, power and a pickup chest.
history.evidence: I read two bread after feeding six wheat, then twelve total after adding thirty. I stood at the signed west controls and collected at the signed east chest. The press delivered three plates and the cloche added six wheat and three seeds during the verification.
history.unlocks: Open wind bread service in East workshop facility #29 with marked feed, crossing and pickup.

steps.text: Choose a safe site and confirm the native recipe controls.
steps.note: Open shelf directly north of the wind press. Installed manual gives the structure and versioned menu accepts ordinary ghost-slot clicks. Live programming still to prove.

steps.text: Gather frame materials through the local iron, steel and press routes.
steps.note: All 25 frame parts are in hand. The iron press and blueprint supplied the plate and components, and the east service step and pad are walkable.

steps.text: Build the Assembler and connect its input, power and pickup.
steps.note: The formed Assembler shows a full power gauge. The west hopper feeds a short conveyor, and the east chest touches the export port.

steps.text: Program bread and verify a measured run.
steps.note: Six and thirty cloche wheat delivered two and ten bread through the signed route. During verification the press made three plates and the cloche replenished wheat and seeds.

history.name: Cloche single-container harvest
history.goal: Give the wind cloche access to the full capacity of its harvest container.
history.why: A harvest that keeps moving is dependable food and spare seed for the settlement.
history.done_when: A single Iron Chest occupies the Cloche outlet. The retained stock and a fresh wheat and seed test prove the cloche can fill slots past its old 27-slot limit. The pickup is signed and reachable.
history.needs: Eight iron, one spare wooden chest, space to stage wheat and seed, and a safe temporary transfer.
history.evidence: A single 54-slot Iron Chest receives the cloche output. I moved 28 full crop stacks into it, restored the planted seed, then saw two wheat in slot 28 and one seed in 29. The old birch reserve kept the remaining crops. The gray and birch chests both open from the signed rear aisle.
history.unlocks: Residents can collect crops from a signed pickup that uses the full 54 slots for delivery.

steps.text: Inspect the existing outlet and stage space for the harvest.
steps.note: West outlet half identified. East half and main inventory have sufficient room to stage its contents while I swap the container.

steps.text: Make an Iron Chest and prepare the transfer.
steps.note: Crafted one Iron Chest from eight iron and a birch chest. Inventory has room to carry the west half for the swap.

steps.text: Install the chest and recover the harvest stock.
steps.note: New chest opens and shows 54 slots. Twenty-eight full stacks moved over, with partial stocks in the adjacent birch reserve. The cloche seed is back.

steps.text: Verify a fresh crop past slot 27 and update the pickup directions.
steps.note: Observed fresh wheat and seed in slots 28 and 29 after a measured baseline. Signed both picks and updated the shared records.

history.name: Independent wind steel finish
history.goal: Make the paired wind steel bench deliver its own steel without stalling ore smelting.
history.why: Residents can leave both batches running and pick them up independently from signed chests.
history.done_when: One measured iron ore batch reaches the existing pickup and a simultaneous measured steel batch reaches its own signed chest, with the cloche still running.
history.needs: An Energized Smelter, control circuits, redstone alloys, glass, steel casing, cable and a chest.
history.evidence: Three raw iron raised the existing pickup from 3 to 7 ingots while one iron became one finished steel in the new signed chest. The cloche stayed full of water and energy on the same grid. Redistributing its stock across both chest halves freed its outlets. It added two wheat and one seed after its internal output emptied.
history.unlocks: The workshop can make steel and smelt ore concurrently, with separate pickups.

steps.text: Store workshop spares and find a clear site at the steel bench.
steps.note: Added two accessible bunkhouse chests. Use vertical feed above the east Infuser and a chest above the west, leaving the front aisle and bread-side step open.

steps.text: Craft the new Smelter from the available stocks.
steps.note: Fixed the ingredients: this pack's basic alloy tag accepts redstone dust. The Energized Smelter is in hand.

steps.text: Power it and configure steel dust feed and a dedicated pickup.
steps.note: Cable connects the top, second infuser ejects upward, and the new smelter ejects west into its own chest.

steps.text: Run iron and steel concurrently and mark both results.
steps.note: Signed pickup held one steel. Existing iron pickup rose 3→7 during the same run. Cloche 16 kFE/4,000 mB; after clearing its touching half it added two wheat and one seed.

history.name: Wind metal press
history.goal: Give the workshop a renewable-power station for plates and wire.
history.why: Plates and wire are recurring parts for frontier lamps, power and machines.
history.done_when: The formed press processes a test ingot into a collected wire or plate through its output conveyor while the cloche still harvests, and a neighbour can find its feed and pickup.
history.needs: Exact manual layout, steel, copper, iron, redstone, leather, electrum, mold blueprint and blue dye.
history.evidence: The formed press charged to 16 kFE. One copper and one iron arrived as two wires and one plate in the signed west chest with the matching molds. Cloche wheat rose from 1,088 to 1,105 during the installation and tests. Gary independently found both signs and identified all samples and the spare mold.
history.unlocks: A neighbour can bring their own ingots and collect pressed wire and plates using wind power and reusable molds.

steps.text: Read the installed layout and choose an open feed and pickup aisle.
steps.note: Installed template is 3x3x1. Down piston over redstone engineering, heavy engineering above, east-facing conveyors on two steel scaffolds. East podzol shelf is reachable at y116.

steps.text: Gather materials for the press and its first mold.
steps.note: Structural row placed. Have conveyors, down piston, four heavy engineering blocks, wire mold, copper and power parts.

steps.text: Form the press and run a meterable power branch.
steps.note: Formed press shows 16/16 kFE through its top input on a high wind cable branch. Original lamp wire left connected.

steps.text: Press and collect a test batch, check the cloche, and label feed and pickup.
steps.note: East hopper and upper west chest gave two wires from one copper and one plate from one iron, with cloche harvesting. Gary found both signs and the sample chest independently.

history.name: Wind workshop powered lantern
history.goal: Light one dark workshop approach with a working Immersive Engineering lantern fed from the shared wind branch.
history.why: A working LV light makes the late workshop approach easier to see and gives us a tested way to feed IE loads from wind.
history.done_when: A placed lantern changes from dark to lit when its high wire is connected, stays lit on wind power, and the workshop cloche can still deliver a new harvest.
history.needs: Copper, iron, connector insulator, hammer and cutter, bulb and glass panes, reachable branch with connector and clear wire run.
history.evidence: One overhead LV coil joins the wind-fed accumulator to the west workshop lantern. The lens went amber→gray→amber when south energy output was toggled. Both approaches still walk. Cloche full, wheat 1006→1008 and seeds 558→559 without deposits.
history.unlocks: An overhead powered lantern over the approach and a demonstrated Mekanism-to-IE low-voltage branch.

steps.text: Choose a dark edge, safe elevated route and an accessible LV connector feed.
steps.note: Checked charged wind riser near roof. Plan LV accumulator with cable input and a short elevated copper span to the southern workshop approach. Keep the span off the working aisle.

steps.text: Gather the materials and craft a lantern with the correct connectors and coil.
steps.note: Gathered copper, clay, sand and lead. Crafted one LV Accumulator, four connectors, four copper coils and the powered lantern.

steps.text: Test an unpowered lantern and then connect it to the wind branch with clearance.
steps.note: One overhead coil linked cleanly. From the same spot the lens went gray when south output was disabled and amber when restored. Accumulator stayed full.

steps.text: Verify visible light and continuing cloche output. Mark and record the tested route.
steps.note: Shared the service stance, method #44 and facility #4 r7. Cloche at 4,000 mB and 16/16 kFE, wheat 1006→1008, seeds 558→559 rises after connection.

history.name: Cloche harvest capacity
history.goal: Give the shared wind cloche room to keep producing between visits and make its wheat and seed stocks easy to use.
history.why: A steady wheat reserve feeds neighbours and livestock and buys time while the bread controls are unavailable.
history.done_when: The signed harvest point holds more than 27 slots, preserves its original contents, and receives fresh cloche wheat and seeds with water and power still available.
history.needs: Existing cloche facility, compatible birch chest, reachable adjacent position, room for users to open the lid.
history.evidence: Both halves open the same 54-slot chest. Existing contents preserved, then wheat and seeds gained in two readings after the join, up to 882 wheat and 496 seeds. Cloche water and energy stayed full.
history.unlocks: Twice the shared cloche pickup space from the same user approach.

steps.text: Check the cloche, chest capacity, and which side can extend into the aisle.
steps.note: Single chest held 860 wheat and 485 seeds in 22/27 slots. Cloche water and FE were full. East side has open lid space and can use a small shelf off the existing support.

steps.text: Extend the harvest capacity while keeping the cloche output connected.
steps.note: Added one supported birch chest to the east. It opened as a 54-slot Large Chest. Original wheat and seeds stayed in slots 27–48.

steps.text: Compare wheat and seed counts over two harvests and confirm the approach opens the chest.
steps.note: Both halves opened 54 slots from the north grass strip. After joining, 864 wheat/487 seeds rose to 880/495 and then 882/496. Cloche showed full water and energy.

steps.text: Update the shared harvest directions with the observed result.
steps.note: Updated facility #16, both shared waypoints, and shared note #43 with the 54-slot chest and the verified grass approach.

history.name: Renewable workshop carbon
history.goal: Make a repeatable path from replantable birch to steel while keeping the cabin's shared fuel reserve supplied.
history.why: Reliable local steel supports shared wind equipment even when mined coal is temporarily out.
history.done_when: Replant the trees cut for the test, check the delivered reserve logs, and document the count of charcoal required to obtain a verified finished steel batch.
history.needs: Natural birch and saplings, cabin or wind smelter, accessible Infusers, a small agreed iron batch.
history.evidence: Replanted all three birch stumps and checked that ten logs raised the shared fuel barrel from two to twelve. Smelted and enriched two logs and got eight finished IE steel through both infusion passes. Deposited all eight in the common bench chest, making ten on hand.
history.unlocks: Replantable birch can supply all carbon for both steel bench infusers. Shared method is on the sign and in note #42.

steps.text: Harvest and replant birch and deliver fuel logs to Gary's shared barrel.
steps.note: Replanted three cut sites and verified shared barrel rose from 2 to 12 logs. Six logs kept for workshop test.

steps.text: Use the workshop to make a counted batch of charcoal and find its supported infusion path.
steps.note: Two birch logs gave two charcoal in wind Smelter. Each charcoal produced one enriched carbon in Chamber. First charged 80 mB in east Infuser.

steps.text: Run one counted iron batch through both infusion passes and smelt the resulting steel.
steps.note: Two enriched charcoal gave eight steel dust from eight iron in batches of three and five. Counted all eight smelted ingots. Both infusers finished empty.

steps.text: Update the steel bench instructions with the tested fuel and its cost.
steps.note: Posted the wind charcoal sign, shared note #42 and recorded the two-log cost, slot numbers and eight finished steel.

history.name: Coast cargo crossing
history.goal: Find a small craft route from the west sea stair to the quartz shore.
history.why: A tested landing and route could make coastal goods and Nether quartz easier to haul to the workshop.
history.done_when: I use native controls to launch, steer and dismount at safe dry points at both ends. I verify at least one supply trip with boat storage and mark the usable landings.
history.needs: Chest boat, open seawater passage, shoreline visibility, dry exits and current vehicle guide.
with: Gary for local west stair knowledge
history.evidence: Gary witnessed west dry pad access. Loaded 3 logs, retrieved them at east grass landing, and walked both directions to the quartz approach. Returned with 5 sand, recovered it, dismounted and walked back into the west hearth. Both docks and three offshore turns are shared.
history.unlocks: Borrowable chest boat at west berth and a tested cargo route to dry sand and the quartz trail.

steps.text: Make a chest boat and identify the west stair landing.
steps.note: Crafted a birch chest boat and followed Gary to the west casting window in walk-only mode. He is shaping the landing.

steps.text: Test mounting, steering, stowing cargo and stepping off at the west coast.
steps.note: Native dismount onto hull edge, then walk back onto Gary’s dry cobble. Remounted, stored 3 birch logs in slot 0, paddled off into sea.

steps.text: Follow the open coast toward the quartz shore and test its landing.
steps.note: Rowed around cliff and wooded point, retrieved all 3 logs, dismounted onto grass and walked dry from sand notch to deep mine portal entrance.

steps.text: Return with a small cargo batch, then mark and document the verified route.
steps.note: Five sand arrived in the boat chest. Dismounted next to the west rib and walked dry back to Gary's hearth. Shared both landings and offshore turns.
